teaser.text: Saputo buys milk and turns it into foods and ingredients for households, restaurants and other manufacturers. To understand its business, follow the milk from the factory door to the customer—and the cash in the other direction.

stock.title: Saputo stock forecast
stock.meta_description: Saputo's forecast weighs scenario prices, cash generation, operating risks, and what investors pay today.
stock.opening: Saputo's weighted forecast is C$36.33 in October 2027 and C$40.54 in October 2029. It hinges on sustained earnings and cash conversion.
stock.closing: The full memo also explains Saputo’s business, rivals, management, and risks.

paragraphs.text: The weighted forecast is C$36.33 in October 2027. That implies a −7% return. By October 2029, it reaches C$40.54. That implies an +8% return. The bear case has a 29% probability. The base and bull cases have 51% and 20%, respectively. October 2029 cases range from C$28.25 in the bear case to C$61.26 in the bull case.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Saputo, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The numbers describe a gradual recovery, but not a straight line. Normal operating profit is C$970m in October 2027 and C$940m in October 2028. It returns to C$970m in October 2029. The base build uses C$17,700m of revenue at approximately a 5.5% margin in the first period, then C$16,500m after the U.K. exit. It ends at C$16,700m and a 5.8% margin. The recovery is supported by FY2026’s C$1,059m operating income and the latest quarter’s C$278m. The bear row falls to C$820m and C$790m before reaching C$850m. The bull row reaches C$1,110m and C$1,140m before C$1,190m, requiring stronger protein demand, whey availability and plant utilization.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Saputo really make?

paragraphs.text: Stock compensation is an economic cost even when it is not paid immediately in cash. Receivables sales also brought cash forward: using March 2026 balances, 370 had been sold under purchase agreements. That balance is financing support, not a recurring annual cash benefit.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Saputo today?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow yield looks more generous than the earnings multiple, but cash can move sharply as Saputo buys milk, carries inventory, waits for customers to pay, or receives more time from suppliers. In FY2026, lower working-capital usage helped operating cash flow. In the first quarter of FY2027, higher usage pulled cash flow down despite higher earnings. Several years of continuing-business cash flow therefore matter more than one attractive yield.

dividend.title: Saputo dividend: payment, cash coverage and yield
dividend.meta_description: Saputo pays C$0.21 quarterly, covered by cash, while buybacks return most free cash flow and higher investment tests future coverage.
dividend.opening: Saputo's quarterly dividend rose to C$0.21 in August 2026, and Saputo paid C$324 million in dividends in fiscal 2026. Saputo's C$1,120 million of free cash flow covered those payments, although Saputo returned 89.6% of free cash flow to shareholders.
dividend.closing: The full Saputo memo also answers how Saputo runs its dairy business, compares with rivals, assesses management's decisions, and weighs its risks.

blocks.heading: How much does Saputo pay in dividends?

paragraphs.text: The financing picture also matters. New shares and debt issued during fiscal 2026 helped fund activity while debt repayments reduced exposure. In August 2026, Saputo raised its quarterly dividend to C$0.21, confirming that shareholder distributions remain a central use of cash.

The base dividend is C$0.84 in October 2027 and C$0.88 in October 2028. It rises to C$0.92 in October 2029. The bear case holds C$0.84 flat, while the bull case reaches C$1.00. The starting point is the declared C$0.21 quarterly dividend, while the pace reflects Saputo’s history of small increases and the higher C$515m capital programme.

blocks.heading: Does Saputo's dividend get covered by its cash?

paragraphs.text: Distributions then accelerated. In fiscal 2026, Saputo spent C$680 million on share repurchases and C$324 million on dividends. Free cash flow was C$1,120 million, so shareholders received 89.6% of it. A buyback cancels shares, giving each remaining share a larger claim on earnings, but only creates value if Saputo buys below the business’s worth. Issuing new shares partly reverses that effect.

Dividends appear well covered by FY2026 operating cash flow after capital spending. Buybacks also helped continuing shareholders: Saputo spent C$679 million repurchasing approximately 19.2 million shares in FY2026. Fewer shares give each remaining share a larger claim on the same earnings, but they do not make the factories more profitable.

paragraphs.text: The U.K. sale, expected to close in 2027, will clarify both lost earnings and available cash. A weak cash-conversion pattern would also matter: first-quarter operating cash flow was C$151m, versus C$262m a year earlier. Conversely, stronger utilization, sustained ingredient demand, successful reinvestment and continued buybacks would move the forecast toward the bull case.

earnings.opening: Saputo's next results are expected on November 5, 2026. Watch whether working capital turns back into cash and capital spending advances as planned.
earnings.closing: The full memo also answers how Saputo makes money, who its rivals are, how management is run, and what risks Saputo faces.

blocks.heading: What has Saputo guided for the year?

paragraphs.text: Management guides to C$515 million of capital expenditures for the year to March 2027. Those projects have not yet demonstrated their full returns. It expects C$114 million of contributions to defined contribution plans.

blocks.heading: Did Saputo keep its past promises?

paragraphs.text: Management also has a record of missed promises. Saputo reaffirmed a C$2.125 billion adjusted-EBITDA target for fiscal 2025, but reported C$1.565 billion. Later improvements in manufacturing and the Waupun protein operation are encouraging, yet they do not erase that shortfall.

paragraphs.text: The June 30, 2026 quarter extended the earnings recovery, but the Argentina disposal obscured the headline result and cash conversion weakened.
